method: Desk research on vendor pages opened 2026-09-24, plus prices already graded in evidence.json. 'claimed' means the vendor says it; we did not use or audit the product. Only PolySync's 'yes' values come from our own CI.

interference.label: Interference-aware
interference.description: Schedules strength and endurance to limit interference

readiness.label: Readiness-adaptive
readiness.description: Adapts the plan to readiness or recovery signals

coachInLoop.label: Coach in the loop
coachInLoop.description: A human coach reviews what the software cannot resolve

auditable.label: Auditable
auditable.description: Publishes its rules and safety evals, so a club can audit why a plan was given

competitors.name: PolySync
competitors.note: Routing to a coach is built; the coach console is not (GAPS #13)

competitors.name: Hypla
competitors.note: Says it never schedules heavy lifting after a long run

competitors.name: HybridX
competitors.note: Garmin two-way sync; 'coach chat' is in-app

competitors.name: Athletica
competitors.note: Closest overall: HRV readiness plus strength-run sequencing

competitors.name: Strava + Runna
competitors.note: Running plans; strength is not scheduled against runs

competitors.name: Ladder
competitors.note: Team programmes led by a coach, not individual review

competitors.name: TrainHeroic
competitors.note: Delivers the coach's plan; the trade-off is the coach's job

competitors.name: ABC Trainerize
competitors.note: Generic AI workout builder; paid add-ons for payments and nutrition

competitors.name: FITR
competitors.note: 'Fitr AI' for programming; markets to HYROX coaches

competitors.name: Future
competitors.note: Dropped its AI coaching beta in Jun 2026

finding: Interference-aware scheduling is no longer a differentiator: three consumer apps at $9-10 a month claim it. No product we checked combines a club buyer, a coach in the loop and rules plus safety evals a club can audit. That combination, not the scheduler, is what PolySync sells (ADR-009).
